requiredGateCriteria.text: Bad configuration, occupied ports, unavailable broker, and failed protected plugin produce actionable bounded failures.

Simultaneous launches and a crashed startup owner converge on one owned instance. Wrong Docker context, conflicting ports, incompatible versions and partial startup produce bounded, specific diagnostics without deleting volumes, starting a shadow stack or attaching to another user.

assignedFailureRequirements.scenario: Cold launch with no selected instance, then warm launch from another project directory
assignedFailureRequirements.oracle: One owned Compose project reaches actual service and application readiness; the next launch reuses its identity and volumes unchanged. Both display the same scoped status schema.

assignedFailureRequirements.scenario: Two terminals or WSL sessions start together; startup owner crashes mid-boot
assignedFailureRequirements.oracle: One startup owner and one selected instance; waiting callers receive bounded progress or failure. Stale ownership recovery cannot create duplicate stacks or trust an unrelated PID.

assignedFailureRequirements.scenario: Docker or Compose absent, daemon unavailable, permission denied or image pull fails
assignedFailureRequirements.oracle: Bounded actionable diagnostics; no false readiness, privileged installation, secret leakage or retry storm. A later corrected launch can recover without losing data.

assignedFailureRequirements.scenario: Wrong Docker context, another user instance, occupied endpoint or incompatible running release
assignedFailureRequirements.oracle: Reject ambiguous or unauthorized attachment; identify selected context and safe next action. Do not start a shadow stack, mutate a remote daemon, silently upgrade or delete volumes.

assignedFailureRequirements.scenario: Partially started or unhealthy stack; readiness timeout; restart after persistent data was written
assignedFailureRequirements.oracle: Report the failing service and observed readiness state. Compatible owned recovery retains instance identity and durable data; unsafe recovery stops for a deliberate action. Running containers alone never qualify success.
